item.title: Re: why are they trying to kill it
item.content:encoded: Some suspect that there is some dark secret about 682 not mentioned in the file that gives the foundation some ulterior motive for wanting to kill it. Not sure what that secret would be, but if (as many suspect) 682 is the offspring of SCP-231-4 it might know what Procedure 110-Montauk is or isn’t, which is certainly grounds for termination. In any case, there is clearly more to the lizard than meets the eye, as one of the earliest tests in the termination log was with SCP-689, an anomaly that only kills humans. The foundation wouldn’t have tested that if they hadn’t already known that it might work, implying not only that 682 is or was a human but also that the O5 council knows that.

item.title: Re: why are they trying to kill it

There's also the fact that it escapes regularly and kills a bunch of people even if they don't try to kill it, so it's worth a shot on the off chance that something works.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
I'm not really fan of this new picture.

First because it looks way too calm and bucolic. It clashes with the idea of a breach, and the framing doesn't help. This is too clean, too posed to be a photo taken right behind a dangerous creature that just went on a rampage.

Second, I don't think the Foundation have an interest in putting this photo in particular. A photo is meant to be useful, to complete the description. What's the point then, if the only visible thing is a barely identifiable back ? If they want a picture to complete the report, then they will take the most useful one. The choice of this one doesn't make sense from the perspective of researchers, even if it's really nice from the point of view of an artist.
Images have a meaning in the context of an SCP, and in my opinion this one misses the point.

But yeah, it's a cool picture…
